title: Recommendation triage panel — WIP UX notes and backlog
content:
Purpose:

Capture a compact, user-centered design direction for a Recommendation Triage Panel inside Optimize that helps engineers and SREs review automated suggestions (batching, caching, quantization), triage which ones to apply, and understand unit-economics impact before committing config changes.

Background / motivation:
- Optimize currently surfaces heuristic suggestions (e.g., enable KV-caching for route X, lower max_batch_size for short sequences). Teams want a single place to: compare predicted latency/cost deltas, inspect quality risk for each rec, and stage rollouts (canary/beta).
- Existing wireframes are fragmented (individual suggestion cards in a modal, separate cost table page). This doc proposes a unified panel that sits on route/config pages and can also be opened as a full-screen review flow.

Primary personas:
- ML/Inference Engineer (fast decisions, cares about correctness & latency)
- Platform/Infra Engineer (cost, capacity, safety nets)
- Product Engineer / Feature Owner (wants simple guidance and easy rollback)

Problem statement:
Engineers are getting a noisy stream of Optimize recs without clear prioritization or economic tradeoffs. They need: relative expected savings, risk indicators (regressions), and an action flow (apply / schedule / reject) that integrates with rollouts.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Reduce time-to-decision for a batch of recs by 50% for typical route owners.
2) Increase adoption of safe recs (low-quality risk + >20% cost delta) by 30% in first month after launch.
3) Provide audit trail + config diff for every applied suggestion.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Predictions of cost/latency are probabilistic and come from service-sim; must show confidence bands.
- Quality regression estimates are heuristics based on eval seed prompts; show sample prompts and scores.
- Must be readable inside Console without long loading (server precompute recommended).

Proposed components (panel-level):
- Header with filter bar: scope (route / model / org), risk filter (low/medium/high), status (pending/applied/rejected), search.
- Priority ribbon: compact, sortable indicator showing net-saved-usd/day (estimate), risk score (0-100), secondary metric (latency delta ms).
- Suggestion card (row): title, primary action, compact delta stack (cost, latency, quality), short rationale, hover for expanded details.
- Expand flyout: shows full prediction bands, sample evaluation prompts + before/after outputs, config diff (JSON), estimated infra change (GPU hours/day), rollback button.
- Batch actions toolbar: select multiple recs and choose Apply, Schedule rollout, Create PR (for Private), Export CSV, Mark as False Positive.
- Audit log & preview: side-pane showing which routes will be affected, estimated percent of traffic impacted, and a simple canary toggle.

Wireframe notes (low-fi description for design):
1) Inline compact view (default) — appears on route configuration page as a collapsible 460px high panel. Each card is a horizontal bar with a left icon (type: batching/caching/quant), mid-text, and right-side action menu. Color coding: green = cost-saver (net savings >10%), amber = neutral/low impact, red = risk-high (quality-risk >60).
2) Full Review mode — full-screen modal with left list and right detail. Left list shows sortable columns (priority, type, est-savings, risk). Right detail renders plots: percentile band for latency, box for token-level quality metric, and a small diffs viewer (config).
3) Rollout scheduler UI — small calendar control + traffic percentage slider (0-100%), with preset buttons: canary-5%, canary-10%, immediate-100%. Must show estimated cumulative savings per step.

Microcopy / UX text suggestions:
- Card title example: "Apply KV-prefix caching for /search (model: rw-v1)"
- Tooltip for savings: "Estimated net savings per day if applied at current traffic — 90% CI shown"
- Risk badge copy: "Quality risk: Medium — sample prompts indicate 2/30 regressions"
- Apply confirmation: "This change will affect ~12% of route traffic. Apply now or schedule a canary rollout?"

Prioritization rules (how to order recs in ribbon):
1) net-saved-usd/day * confidence_multiplier (confidence = 0.8 for >75% CI overlap)
2) reduce latency SLO breaches (if rec reduces p95 by >10% it gets a priority boost)
3) manual star from owner (persisted)

Grooming backlog (candidate tickets) — rough drafts below that should be split into smaller tasks:
- OPT-1123: backend: expose rec bundle endpoint /api/v1/optimize/recs?route_id=xxx — include cost/latency/quality bands and config-diff (est schema).
- OPT-1124: console: triage panel component + list view skeleton + filters. (Design token integration).
- OPT-1125: console: detail flyout with diffs viewer + eval sample UI (render side-by-side outputs).
- OPT-1126: rollout scheduler: frontend + backend scheduling webhook + telemetry events.
- OPT-1127: experiments: ab test ordering by economic impact vs. ordering by risk-first.
- OPT-1128: infra: daily precompute job for predictions + cache TTL policy.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Users can open panel from route page and see at least 5 recs with populated predictions.
- Multi-select batch apply schedules a rollout job and emits telemetry OPT.SUGGESTION.APPLY with ids.
- Detail flyout shows config diff and sample prompt responses for each rec.
- All applied recs record an audit entry with owner, timestamp, and diff.

Open questions / risks (notes-to-self):
- How to display model-variant fallbacks? Should suggestions that change model family be blocked by default?
- Quantization suggestions often have sparse but high-impact regressions; need a better conservative heuristic.
- Performance: can we keep list rendering snappy when there are 100s of recs for org-level view? Consider server-side pagination + client ranking.

Design experiments (ideas for MVP):
- MVP A: Focus on cost-first ordering; hide low-confidence recs behind "show all" toggle.
- MVP B: Risk-first ordering with safety defaults (require manual opt-in for quantization).
- Run both as an experiment targeted at small vs large customers.

Next steps (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: agree API schema + small backend stub (OPT-1123, OPT-1128). Console: list + simple card + basic filters (OPT-1124).
- Sprint 2: detail flyout + rollout scheduler + telemetry events (OPT-1125, OPT-1126).
- Sprint 3: polish microcopy, add audit export, enable canary presets, run 2-week pilot with two internal teams.

Sketch assets / references (temp links):
- rough sketch: https://figma.com/file/small-slab/reco-triage-v1 (placeholder)
- earlier recommendation notes: confluence: OPT-420-recs-overview

Misc notes (voice of doc):
- Keep the panel focused on "decide quickly" — UI density should favor one-line decisions with an easy path to deep-dive.
- Avoid adding too many toggles on the card; keep complex controls inside the flyout.

"This is a WIP doc — use as source for grooming session on 2025-02-15. Add screenshots and link experiments back to linked_artifacts above."
